# Issue labels

Repository maintainers should create and apply the following labels in GitHub. The prefixes keep filtering and automation predictable.

| Label | Use |
| --- | --- |
| `kind: bug` | A reproducible defect. |
| `kind: feature` | A proposed user-facing capability. |
| `kind: documentation` | Documentation-only change or issue. |
| `kind: question` | A bounded question that belongs in Issues; broad questions belong in Discussions. |
| `area: strategy` | Requirement and strategy system. |
| `area: creative` | Creative system. |
| `area: insights` | Asset intelligence and analytics system. |
| `area: delivery` | Governed delivery system. |
| `area: platform` | Shared foundation, API, identity, agent, provider, media, or audit work. |
| `area: docs` | Repository, product, design, or technical documentation. |
| `priority: critical` | Security, data loss, or a release-blocking issue. |
| `priority: high` | Significant user, correctness, or roadmap impact. |
| `priority: normal` | Important but not urgent. |
| `status: needs-triage` | Newly reported; maintainer review needed. |
| `status: needs-info` | Reporter input required before work can continue. |
| `status: accepted` | Accepted for planning or implementation. |
| `status: blocked` | Waiting on a dependency or decision. |
| `good first issue` | Small, bounded task suitable for a first contribution. |
| `help wanted` | Maintainers welcome external help. |
| `security` | Security-sensitive item; do not use for undisclosed vulnerabilities. |

Labels document intent only; they do not replace the governance or security process.
